faqs.question: What do you write in a Halloween note to your neighbors?
faqs.answer: Give the note one job, such as a welcome, a party warning, a thank-you or an apology, and put it in the first line. Sign with your name and door number and offer one way to reply. For a text, keep it to two lines, since 48.3% of the pages shared through SubhSandesh are opened on a phone.

faqs.question: How do I tell my neighbors I'm not doing trick-or-treat this year?
faqs.answer: Tape a short 'not tonight' sign to your door or window on the afternoon of 31 October and leave the porch light off. New Zealand Police and Cheshire Police in England both publish printable 'No Trick or Treaters Please' posters if you'd rather not write your own.

faqs.question: Does a porch light that is off mean no trick-or-treaters?
faqs.answer: In the US and Canada it is usually read that way, but it is a custom, not a rule. Many people leave a light on just to see who is at the door, so a written sign is the only signal nobody can misread.

faqs.question: How far ahead should I warn neighbors about a Halloween party?
faqs.answer: Two days ahead is a good rule. For a Friday party on 30 October 2026, deliver the note on Thursday 29 October; for a Saturday party on 30 October 2027, deliver it on Thursday 28 October, and include an end time and a phone number.

faqs.question: What time should a Halloween party in an apartment end?
faqs.answer: In England and Wales, the Noise Act 1996 treats 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. as night hours, when councils may investigate complaints about excessive noise from a home, so ending by 11 is the safe choice. In the US, quiet hours are set by each city or county and often by your lease, so check both.

faqs.question: Should I give a new neighbor something for Halloween?
faqs.answer: A small treat bag with a short welcome note is an easy opener, and Halloween gives you a reason to knock. A 2023 BMJ Open survey of 639 Delhi residents found the sense of neighborhood cohesion grew with length of residence, so newcomers have the most to gain.

faqs.question: How do I thank a neighbor for their Halloween decorations?
faqs.answer: Leave a one- or two-sentence card in their mailbox the day after, Sunday 1 November 2026 or Monday 1 November 2027. Name one specific thing, such as the fog machine or the glowing pumpkins, so it reads as noticed rather than polite.

faqs.question: What should I say to an elderly neighbor on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Offer something concrete, such as a sign that turns callers away or help with errands, and make it easy to say no. A 2026 study of 7,879 US adults found neighborhood cohesion lowered loneliness only for some groups, so treat the note as a door-opener rather than a fix.

faqs.question: How do I apologize to a neighbor after something goes wrong on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Knock within 24 hours, and leave a note if nobody answers. Say what happened in one sentence and offer a specific fix, such as replacing a pumpkin or the trampled plants.

faqs.question: Can I send a neighbor a Halloween card online instead?
faqs.answer: Yes, for one person you know well, such as a neighbor who became a friend and moved away. The SubhSandesh Halloween card takes about 5 minutes and the premium page about 10, but both ask "Will you be my boo?" by default, so rewrite the question for a neighbor; neither is meant for messaging a whole street.

faqs.question: When is Halloween in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween is always 31 October. It falls on a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027, so parties usually move to Friday 30 October 2026 or Saturday 30 October 2027.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Messages for Neighbors: 7 Notes, Each With One Job

The best Halloween messages for neighbors are short, signed notes with one job each: welcome someone new, say whether you're handing out treats, warn about a party, thank a decorator, check on an older neighbor or apologize. Put the job in the first line and add your door number. If you text it, keep it to two lines: 48.3% of the pages shared through SubhSandesh are opened on a phone.

Timing matters as much as wording. In our nearest analogue, Raksha Bandhan 2026 (a different festival, and only 89 pages), 49.4% of greeting pages were built on the festival day itself. Late suits a thank-you, not a party warning, so below are 30 original lines by purpose, plus a delivery calendar for 31 October 2026 (Saturday) and 2027 (Sunday).

## What should a Halloween note to neighbors say?

A Halloween message for neighbors is a short, friendly note telling the people next door something useful about 31 October: less a greeting card than a doorstep courtesy. Sign it with a name and door number (anonymous treats belong to the boo game) and give one way to reply.

Sociologists call a street's readiness to look out for each other "collective efficacy". A [2012 Journal of Aging Research study of 1,151 Chicago adults aged 65 to 95](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC3270404) by Galinsky, Cagney and Browning measured it alongside everyday exchange between neighbors: doing favors, watching absent neighbors' homes, asking advice and visiting. A Halloween note is one of those small exchanges.

## Welcome-to-the-street Halloween notes for a new neighbor

Newcomers start behind: in a [2023 BMJ Open survey of 639 residents in two Delhi settlements](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10580277), Humble and colleagues found that longer residence went with a stronger sense of neighborhood cohesion (r = 0.157 and 0.171), and cohesion tracked well-being (r = 0.145 and 0.264). The correlations are modest, but Halloween gives you a reason to knock. Tape one of these to a small treat bag:

- "Welcome to [street name]! Halloween here means a busy doorstep from about 5:30, so consider this your warning, plus a few sweets for the early callers."
- "Hi from number [12]. If you'd like to join in on 31 October, most houses here leave a pumpkin out. If not, nobody on this street will mind."
- "We're the [surname]s, two doors down, with a dog who barks at capes. Knock if you need anything, costume emergencies included."
- "Welcome! If Halloween isn't your thing, a 'not tonight' sign on the door works perfectly here, and the families on this street respect it."

## "We're handing out" and "not tonight" door signs

A door sign answers before anyone knocks. In North America a lit porch light is read as "come up" and a dark one as "pass by", but that is a custom rather than a rule, and many people leave one on simply to see who's outside.

[New Zealand Police published two posters in 2015](https://www.police.govt.nz/node/39433), "Trick or Treaters Welcome" and "No Trick or Treaters Please", and reminded householders they don't have to answer the door. In England, [Warrington Borough Council shares Cheshire Police posters](https://www.warrington.gov.uk/halloween-safety) (page dated 16 September 2026) and asks children to take "no" for an answer. Four for an open door:

- "Knock away! Treats at this door from 6 to 8 pm. Happy Halloween from apartment [4B]."
- "Friendly ghosts live here. Please knock gently, there's a baby asleep downstairs."
- "Brave enough to ring? Say the magic words and take two."
- "Costumes admired, jokes rewarded, treats guaranteed. Come on up."

Four for a closed one, plus one allergy line (a teal pumpkin on the step says the same in North America):

- "Not tonight, ghouls! We're sitting this Halloween out. Have a brilliant night."
- "No treats here this year, but plenty of goodwill. Happy haunting on the rest of the street."
- "Please don't knock: someone here is unwell and resting. Thanks for understanding, little ghosts."
- "We don't celebrate Halloween, but we hope your night is safe and fun. Please skip our door."
- "Two bowls tonight: candy on the left, non-food treats on the right for anyone with allergies."

## Party and noise heads-up notes for apartment neighbors

A heads-up note turns a noise complaint into a shrug, if it arrives early. In the same Raksha Bandhan 2026 analogue (n = 89, too small for fine detail), 86.1% of the pages finished in time were built within 24 hours of the day; a party warning that late reads as a done deal. Deliver it two days ahead: Thursday 29 October 2026 for a Friday party, or Thursday 28 October 2027 for a Saturday one.

Name an end time. In England and Wales, section 2 of the Noise Act 1996 defines ["night hours" as 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1996/37/section/2), when a council may investigate a complaint about excessive noise from a home. US cities set their own quiet hours, so check your local code or lease.

- "Fair warning from apartment [3A]: a small Halloween gathering here on [Friday 30 October], 8 to 11 pm. Too loud? Knock or text [number] and the volume drops at once."
- "Halloween party upstairs on [date]! Music off by 11. You're very welcome to drop in, costume optional."
- "Twelve guests, one playlist, finished by 10:30 on [Saturday]. Earplugs attached as a peace offering, just in case."
- "We'll be lively for a few hours on [date] and quiet as a tomb after 11. Here's my number if we're not."

## Thank-you and sorry notes for the neighbors next door

Two notes follow the night itself. Both work best within a day: Sunday 1 November 2026 or Monday 1 November 2027.

### Thank-you notes for a neighbor's Halloween decorations

A thank-you is rarer than the decorations. Leave it in the mailbox:

- "Our kids planned their entire route around your graveyard. Thank you for making 31 October feel like an event."
- "Your fog machine and that cackling witch made our walk home the highlight of the week. Thanks for all the effort."
- "Thank you for the decorations, and for the full-size chocolate bars. You've set a standard the rest of us can't reach."
- "To everyone at number [7]: the glowing pumpkins on your steps made our street look like a postcard."

### Apology notes for lost decorations and Halloween mishaps

Something always goes astray on 31 October. Say sorry within 24 hours and offer a fix:

- "Our inflatable ghost escaped into your yard overnight. Sorry! If it damaged anything, tell us and we'll put it right."
- "Our son knocked over your pumpkin while racing to the next house. He'd like to carve you a new one this weekend, if you'll let him."
- "Has anyone seen a three-foot plastic raven? He left our porch on 31 October and we miss him. Apartment [2C]."
- "Apologies for the trampled border by your path; our trick-or-treaters cut the corner. We'll replace the plants this week."

## Halloween notes for an elderly neighbor living alone

For an older neighbor, the note says someone has noticed them, though how much that helps varies. In [a 2026 Journals of Gerontology analysis of 7,879 midlife and older US adults](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13150446), Stokes and colleagues found neighborhood cohesion linked to lower loneliness only among non-Hispanic White participants, while loneliness tracked faster cognitive decline in every group. Treat it as a door-opener and make "no thanks" easy:

- "Happy Halloween from [name] at number [9]. The doorbell will be busy tonight; if you'd rather not answer, the sign attached will turn the callers away."
- "We're bringing the grandkids round at 6 to wave from the step. If that's not a good time, leave your porch light off and we'll understand."
- "If the knocking gets too much tonight, text me at [number] and I'll stand at your gate and redirect the little monsters."
- "We made far too much pumpkin soup. A jar is by your door, and there's more if you'd like it."
- "I'm going to the shops on Monday, so if you need anything carried back, slip a note through my door."

## Which Halloween note, when and how? 5 notes compared

The table compares the five notes. Each gets a delivery date for both years, a channel and a length:

| Note | Deliver by (2026 / 2027) | Best channel | Length |
|---|---|---|---|
| Welcome | Thu 29 Oct 2026 / Fri 29 Oct 2027 | Card with a small treat, by hand | 2–3 sentences |
| Party heads-up | 48 hours before the party | Under the door, plus the building chat | Date, start, end time, phone number |
| Door sign | Afternoon of Sat 31 Oct 2026 / Sun 31 Oct 2027 | Taped to the door or window | 1 line in large letters |
| Thank-you | Sun 1 Nov 2026 / Mon 1 Nov 2027 | Card in the mailbox | 1–2 sentences |
| Apology | Within 24 hours | Knock first, note if nobody answers | 2 sentences plus a fix |

Only the door sign belongs on the day itself. Anything asking a neighbor to tolerate or join something goes out first.

## A Halloween page for the neighbor who moved away

Most neighbors should get paper. The exception is a neighbor-turned-friend who moved away, and a link gets revisited: the average SubhSandesh page is viewed 11.1 times.

The [interactive Halloween card with a little haunted house](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about 5 minutes, holds up to 6 photos and has a family mode. The [premium Halloween page with a 60-second voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about 10 minutes, holds up to 12 photos and adds an unlock time and a reply box. Both are one-person greeting pages, not street invitations; otherwise, [browse all SubhSandesh templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates).

### When a Halloween page is the wrong choice for a neighbor

Both pages ask "Will you be my boo?" by default, and on the regular card the No button runs away. For a neighbor, rewrite the question (up to 60 characters) as one with no wrong answer, such as "Pumpkin swap again next year?", or pick family mode, where the premium page shows no No button. For an older neighbor without a smartphone, hand-deliver paper instead; the pages are also English-only.

## Sources

- Galinsky, Cagney and Browning, Journal of Aging Research, 23 January 2012.
- Humble and colleagues, BMJ Open, 11 April 2023.
- Stokes and colleagues, Journals of Gerontology Series B, 1 May 2026.
- New Zealand Police, "Safe, scary fun", October 2015.
- Warrington Borough Council, "Halloween safety", 16 September 2026.
- Noise Act 1996, section 2, legislation.gov.uk.

structuralLimitations: No Halloween usage data exists; the lead-time figures are Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n = 89), disclosed in prose as an analogue and as too small for detail.

Porch-light convention: the BRIEF/prompt framing is right that it is a custom, not a rule. A Thames Valley Police alert (seen only as a search snippet; its domain ranks top-5 for this keyword, so not cited) advises keeping an outside light on for safety, which is why the post says many people leave a light on simply to see who is outside and recommends a written sign.
Teal pumpkin is mentioned in one unlinked clause only (owned by b6 teal-pumpkin-project); out-of-candy signs are owned by b4 porch decorations and are not repeated.
Stokes 2026 found cohesion lowered loneliness only for non-Hispanic White participants; the post reports that limit rather than claiming notes reduce loneliness.
legislation.gov.uk HTML returned an error to the fetcher; the section text was read from its data.xml.
No US noise-ordinance source was cited, because quiet hours vary by city; the post tells readers to check their local code or lease.
